solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take out permit to enter river

indicators.note: one word going to enter another is placed inside it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in England, Wales and Scotland
to let is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: An official removes a fishing or building licence so the holder can no longer go into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' looks like a noun, a licence, but it gives the verb let; the Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to remove or strike out, as with text or a record.

clue.text: Present some French support band in church

parts.note: des is French for some

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rib is a supporting band, as in a vault or a boat's frame

explanation.surface: A French act opening for a gig in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support band' suggests a gig's opening act; here it is a rib. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To present an account or picture of something is to describe it, verb for verb.

clue.text: Bloomers on string blowing around in field

indicators.note: going around turns the letters to face the other way
the answer lies inside the next word

parts.note: the middle three letters of field

explanation.surface: Flowers threaded on a cord flap about in the open meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are usually knickers; here they are flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers threaded on a string.

clue.text: Book a time to tour castle and see Measure for Measure?

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so these letters surround another piece

parts.note: Tit is the abbreviation for Titus, a book of the New Testament
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
a fort is a fortified castle

explanation.surface: Reserve a slot to visit a castle and watch a performance of Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's play title is reused for a like-for-like return; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is retaliation in kind, giving back exactly what you received, measure for measure.

clue.text: Object after armed force returned old money

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece second, behind the one that follows it in the clue
something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Something brought back by soldiers turns out to be a coin no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the object behind the reversed air force. A farthing was a quarter of an old British penny, withdrawn in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was a pre-decimal British coin, so it counts as old currency.

clue.text: Butler once visited a cultural centre for a coffee

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited

parts.note: taken as written
Rab Butler was a leading British Conservative politician of the mid-20th century
the ICA is London's Institute of Contemporary Arts

explanation.surface: A former household servant pops into an arts centre's café for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Butler is not a servant but Rab Butler, the mid-century Conservative statesman; the ICA is London's Institute of Contemporary Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is a species of coffee plant and the bean it yields.

clue.text: It's a result when the force captures one!

definitions.text: It's a result when the force captures one!

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
F is the symbol for force in physics
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Police celebrate catching a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a result is slang for a success, and the police force capturing one such person is a good day.
explanation.definitionFit: When the police catch a robber, that is a result in the slang sense of a win.

clue.text: Regiment run off when there's no one in charge

definitions.text: when there's no one in charge

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers flee the field when their commander has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off' reads as fleeing; 'run' is fodder and 'off' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An interregnum is a period between rulers, when power is vacant.

clue.text: Monstrous sister backs order to keep off the booze!

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.words: order to keep off the booze
parts.note: grog is rum and water, so the command is no grog

explanation.surface: A formidable sibling supports a demand to stop drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' looks like supports, but it is the signal to read the order the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorgons were three monstrous sisters of Greek myth, one of them Medusa.

clue.text: Rip off a woolly coat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to swindle or overcharge
second meaning: a sheep's coat of wool, or a soft warm jacket

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tearing off a jumper; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is to cheat someone of money, and a fleece is a sheep's wool or a soft jacket.

clue.text: Hint left in italics confused about term of loan

indicators.note: the jumble goes about, that is around, the single selected letter
confused letters are jumbled out of their proper order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written, to be mixed with the L

indicators.note: a term is an end point, so only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of loan

explanation.surface: A clue printed in sloping type gets muddled around the length of a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: The L goes in with ITALICS to make the anagram fodder; the jumble then wraps around the last letter of loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark of something, much like a hint.

clue.text: Bury drop a point at start of season

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: winter is a season of the year
W, west, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Bury, the Lancashire football club, lose a point on the opening day of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town and football club, which hides the verb. The point dropped is the W that starts WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it in a grave.

clue.text: About to check genuineness of carpet

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to prove something is to verify that it is genuine

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a rug to see whether it is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb here, not the rug: to carpet someone is British slang for calling them in for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to rebuke them, the same as to reprove.

clue.text: Enter an uneasy pact with pirate about India

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumble goes around a letter
something uneasy is unsettled, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone agrees a shaky deal with a buccaneer concerning India.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a race or contest is to take part in it, to participate.

clue.text: Deduce nothing that's new in old poem

parts.note: to infer is to deduce
N is the abbreviation for new
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A reader concludes there is nothing original in an ancient poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The nothing and the new are placed in the order N then O after the deduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is the first part of Dante's medieval Divine Comedy, a centuries-old narrative poem.

clue.text: Make peace — no longer having an axe to grind?

parts.words: no longer having an axe to grind?
parts.note: surface reading: someone has stopped nursing a grievance

parts.words: no longer having an axe to grind?
parts.note: setter's reading: literally the axe has been put in the ground and so is no longer available to sharpen

explanation.walkthrough: An axe to grind is a private grudge; the phrase for ending a quarrel literally involves putting a small axe into the earth, so there is none left to sharpen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to settle a quarrel and make friends again, from a Native American peace custom.

clue.text: Revolting chapati stuffed with a lot of old meat

indicators.note: something stuffed with a filling holds it inside
revolting things rise up and overturn order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most but not all of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A disgusting Indian flatbread filled with lots of stale meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting reads as disgusting but signals the anagram. A chapati is an Indian flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, so a piece of meat.

clue.text: Cut elm behind run-down palace

indicators.note: run-down means dilapidated, out of good order, so the letters are rearranged
something cut is trimmed, so the following word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: An elm tree is felled behind a palace that has fallen into disrepair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut elm' suggests felling the tree, but 'Cut' trims behind instead. Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire was Churchill's birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace is the country seat of the Dukes of Marlborough in Oxfordshire.

clue.text: Police officer has to emphasise extraordinary cry for help

parts.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector
to stress is to emphasise
signal as an adjective means notable or remarkable, as in a signal success

explanation.surface: An inspector must put weight on an unusual shout for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' looks like an anagram signal, but it gives the adjective signal, as in a signal achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: A distress signal, such as an SOS or a flare, is an urgent appeal for rescue.

clue.text: Busy journalist pens new joke at end of article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as in a sheep pen

parts.note: ED is short for editor
N is the abbreviation for new
a gag is a joke

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of article

explanation.surface: A hard-pressed reporter writes a fresh gag to finish a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writing, but it means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or person that is engaged is occupied, so busy.

clue.text: Go off after second joint of meat

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece second, behind the one that follows it in the clue

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
eggs that addle go off, or rot

explanation.surface: A cut of meat starts to rot shortly after it is bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is a butcher's cut from the back of the animal, such as saddle of lamb.

clue.text: Behaves badly when outside court appearing for trial

indicators.note: a word placed outside wraps around another

parts.note: as can mean when
CT is the abbreviation for court
someone up before the judge is appearing in court

explanation.surface: A defendant misbehaves outside the courtroom before a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is a phrasal verb for misbehaving, as children do.

clue.text: Natter with mate outside before start of Glasto

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate
W is an abbreviation for with

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of Glasto

explanation.surface: Chatting with a friend while waiting for Glastonbury festival to open.
explanation.walkthrough: China for mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate). Glasto is the nickname of the Glastonbury music festival in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal British word for a chat, the same as a natter.

clue.text: After wicket, tip spinner

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket
a ship heels when it tips over to one side

explanation.surface: Cricket advice to a spin bowler once a batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' reads as a spin bowler in cricket; it is simply something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is a thing that spins round on an axle.

clue.text: Key staff collect retired bouncer for concierge

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: D is a musical key

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a kangaroo bounces, and roo is its short form
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Important employees bring in a former nightclub heavy to work at a hotel desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' tempts as the definition, but here it is the kangaroo, reversed and held between key and staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman attends the entrance of a hotel or apartment block, which is a concierge's role.

clue.text: Gone off story after its introduction

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece second, behind the single letter that follows it in the clue
an introduction is the opening, and its points back to the word just named, so only that word's first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of story
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A narrative goes downhill once its opening section is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The story's own first letter is placed before the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is no longer fresh, which is what stale means.

clue.text: Fire and strong wind traps vehicle one's following

indicators.note: something that traps another holds it inside

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: one piece following another is placed directly after it

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
one is I, and I'S is one's

explanation.surface: A blaze and a gale together trap a vehicle with someone close behind.
explanation.walkthrough: One's gives I'S, which follows the van inside the gale.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to galvanise them, stirring them into action.

clue.text: Unkind millionaire has it both ways

indicators.note: a word that has something holds it within its letters

parts.note: letters two to four of millionaire
surface padding with a wink: the same letters also appear reversed inside the word

explanation.surface: A cruel rich person gets things whichever way they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It both ways' adds that the letters also appear reading backwards within the same word, as LLI before the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as an adjective can mean harsh or hostile, as in ill will or ill treatment.

clue.text: Rule out overture without leader of cellists

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece, like an overture

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of cellists

explanation.surface: An opening piece is cancelled because the principal cellist is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', which would remove a letter; it means outside, so the C goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent it or make it impossible, so to rule it out.

clue.text: Left group of women outside part of Manhattan

indicators.note: a word placed outside another wraps around it

parts.note: a harem is a group of women in a household
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A man departed while the women waited outside a district of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is a neighbourhood in northern Manhattan, New York City.
